question: Where is the DEEPEST lake on Earth?

post.premise: 1,642 m deep and a fifth of Earth's fresh water in one lake
post.bait: Russia, Tanzania or the USA — which did you pick? 👇
post.sources_line: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, NASA Earth Observatory, Britannica, Wikipedia

research.topic: Where is the deepest lake on Earth? (Lake Baikal, Russia — 1,642 m)

myths.myth: The Caspian Sea or Lake Superior is the deepest lake.
myths.reality: Baikal is deepest at 1,642 m; Tanganyika is second (1,470 m); Superior is 406 m; the Caspian's maximum is 1,025 m.

landscape.our_gap: Feed answers say 'Baikal' over a stock photo; nobody puts depth, the 20 % water share, the age, and the one outflow on the actual lake outline.

unesco_baikal.title: Lake Baikal
unesco_baikal.notes: inscribed 1996; oldest (25 million years) and deepest (1,700 m) lake; 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater reserve; endemic Baikal seal (nerpa)

nasa_eo.title: Lake Baikal, Russia
nasa_eo.notes: deepest lake, ~1,600+ m; holds about 20 percent of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water; ~25 million years old

britannica_baikal.title: Lake Baikal
britannica_baikal.notes: deepest continental body of water, max depth 1,620 m (5,315 ft) [older figure]; 336 rivers feed it, the Angara is the sole outlet; 25 million years old; Baikal seal endemic; one-fifth of Earth's fresh surface water

wiki_baikal.title: Lake Baikal
wiki_baikal.notes: max depth 1,642 m (5,387 ft); 23,615 km³ ≈ 22–23 % of the world's fresh surface water; 25–30 million years old; 330+ inflowing rivers, outflow only the Angara; Baikal seal; Olkhon largest island; UNESCO 1996

wiki_deep.title: List of lakes by depth
wiki_deep.notes: 1 Baikal 1,642 m (Russia); 2 Tanganyika 1,470 m; 3 Caspian 1,025 m; Crater Lake (USA) 594 m deepest in the US

bbc_baikal.title: Lake Baikal: the world's oldest and deepest lake
bbc_baikal.notes: 1,642 m deep; ~20% of unfrozen fresh water; 25 million years old; nerpa seal endemic; Angara the only outlet
